prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation; Airline Operations Coordinator may propose revision for cleaning/restoration delay. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode (reduced remote stands, shorter sweep intervals); Capacity Reduction State (Airport Duty Manager may declare localized for apron contamination/closures; tighter escalation); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Contingency Operations Console). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; Tactical Regulation Proposal); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time, retained until delay exceeds Registry tolerance; evaluates swaps vs Ground Delay Program, CTT, TOBT, AAR); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; suppresses release if stand not ready or route blocked); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; readiness confirmations; slot swap entry: flight IDs, reason, readiness basis, effective time; validates via Identity Access Service, blocks non-delegated parties); Collaborative Decision Log; Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft without remote stand release); Gate Conflict Detector (readiness vs allocation, towing, adjacent occupancy); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency; to Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh within 5 s; states unchecked/under inspection/cleaned/blocked/ready); Common Situation Display; Audit Event Ledger (readiness changes, acknowledgements, hazard closures, releases); Business Rules Registry (precedence, equity, customs, notification time, prohibited trades); Identity Access Service; Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet); Flight Data Exchange; Performance Analytics Warehouse (aggregated readiness/debris patterns); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Data Governance Steward; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison. Apron: readiness prerequisite for release, not movement clearance (Tower Supervisor);

Document units:
S671: The Slot Coordinator reviews any exception raised by the Slot Allocation Engine and confirms whether the swap remains consistent with regional flow objectives.
S672: Slot Coordinator sends the Slot Swap Permission Email only after the governance checks have been completed and recorded.
S673: For airline-to-airline coordination, each Aircraft Operator Representative records concurrence in the Airport CDM Portal rather than relying on a verbal agreement.
S674: The Network Operations Liaison monitors aggregate displacement from approved substitutions to ensure that one carrier's recovery action does not destabilize the wider network plan.
S675: The Regional Flow Manager may suspend collaborative substitution during a Capacity Reduction State when scarce capacity must be protected for the published tactical plan.
S676: The Tower Supervisor retains authority to reject a swap if the resulting sequence would conflict with safe runway sequencing or local control workload.
S677: The Ramp Control Lead confirms that the revised sequence remains compatible with stand occupancy, pushback spacing, and tug availability shown on the Ramp Movement Board.
S678: Airport Duty Manager uses the Apron Sweep Completion Note to confirm that apron availability constraints do not invalidate an approved substitution.
S679: Airline Operations Coordinator uses the release note to confirm that a candidate substitution is eligible for customs release before requesting a slot swap.
S680: Customs release status is treated as a prerequisite condition for any substitution that would move an international departure into an earlier operating position.
S681: If customs status is incomplete, the Airport CDM Portal keeps the proposal pending and prevents the Slot Allocation Engine from publishing the revised slot assignment.
S682: The Collaborative Decision Log captures the proposed flights, the reason code, the user confirmations, the governance outcome, and the final decision time.
S683: The Audit Event Ledger records each approval, rejection, cancellation, and override so that later review can distinguish operational judgment from system enforcement.
S684: The Flight Data Exchange publishes revised Flight Intent Message content only after the approved substitution is final and time synchronized.
S685: The Common Situation Display presents the updated Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time so that operational users share the same view of the accepted change.
S686: The Departure Metering Service recalculates metering advisories after approval and prevents the swap from creating a new demand peak at a departure fix.
S687: Disputes between operators are escalated to the Regional Flow Manager when the recorded concurrences conflict or when a party alleges that governance rules were bypassed.
